weighting_policy.policy: Intrinsic judgment and collision evidence remain separate. A direct collision can prevent selection, but namespace cleanliness cannot repair a weak identity and distant use is not an automatic veto.

intrinsic_review.comparison_to_dsx: Imp is stronger as a memorable, speakable, extensible master brand and as Elixir code nomenclature. DSX is stronger only as literal DSPy-lineage shorthand.
strengths: The name works as an ordinary word without requiring an acronym.
Imp embedded in self-improving preserves the original concept without copying DSPy's surface form.
Imp, :imp, mix imp.*, IMP_*, and [:imp] form one compact identity grammar.
The descriptor states the category while the brand carries personality and recall.
The word can extend naturally across optimizer, evaluation, runtime, artifact, research, and hosted-product surfaces.
risks: The primary noun senses are a small demon and a mischievous child, which can suggest playfulness or uncontrolled behavior.
The name alone does not communicate Elixir, language-model programs, or production rigor.
Capital I can resemble lowercase l in some typefaces.
The very short common word is intrinsically difficult to search for and own broadly.

market_and_ecosystem_observations.observation: An active exact-name repository uses imp for a C++/CUDA inference engine aimed at agentic AI. It was created in February 2026 and reports a substantial implementation and benchmark surface.

A February 2026 Python project brands itself imp and describes an AI-powered engineering workflow framework for planning, validation, review, and metrics. Its PyPI package is impx and its observed public footprint is very small.
Imp is the published name of a family of efficient large multimodal models with released training and evaluation code.
Electric Imp is an active edge-to-cloud IoT platform and uses imp for its hardware modules and impOS software.
IMP is an active open-source C++ and Python Integrative Modeling Platform for biomolecular modeling.
IMP is a conventional name for small imperative languages in programming-language education and research, and LiSA maintains a concrete IMP test language.
Python's imp standard-library module was deprecated in Python 3.4 and removed in Python 3.12, but remains familiar to the DSPy-adjacent audience and dominates some searches.
Several active software and AI uses create common-law and search-confusion questions. No comprehensive federal, state, international, company-name, or common-law clearance was performed.

older_senses: to graft or repair a bird's feather to improve flight
linguistic_observations.interpretation: The mischievous reading adds memorable character but can weaken enterprise trust. The older repair-and-flight sense is unusually aligned with measured program improvement, though too obscure to carry the public explanation.

independent_review.summary: The reviewer found Imp materially stronger than DSX as a master brand and code namespace, while requiring qualified legal review, permanent descriptor use, and deliberate trust framing.
independent_review.correction: The reviewer suggested preserving broad DSEx compatibility. The repository audit contradicts that generic recommendation: the project is private, pre-release, untagged, and unpublished on Hex, so only persisted-artifact readers warrant targeted compatibility.

recommendation.decision: Imp works as the Elixir package and is preferred to DSX. It is not a clean or exclusive master-brand namespace because active exact-name AI projects exist.
go_conditions: The owner knowingly accepts a shared and crowded software identity rather than requiring broad exclusivity.
A qualified legal review finds no blocking likelihood-of-confusion issue in the intended jurisdictions and goods or services.
The descriptor Declarative self-improving Elixir accompanies the brand on first-contact surfaces.
A small listener set does not consistently interpret the name as unsafe, unserious, or as the existing AI inference engine.
The final identity record uses Imp as a word and does not invent a required acronym expansion.
no_go_conditions: The master brand must be broadly ownable across AI infrastructure, developer tools, and future hosted services.
Qualified review finds the active exact-name software uses materially confusing.
Target users consistently reject the mischievous or demonic connotation.

limitations: This is a targeted public-web and registry screen, not legal advice or trademark clearance.
No native-speaker, international community, assistive-technology, or statistically meaningful listener study was performed.
Repository counts and project activity can change after the observation time.
Domain and social-handle availability was not used as decision evidence.
